attacks.claim: The PR says truncation 'only cuts at whitespace or between tokens', but the fallback branch hard-cuts a leading unbroken word mid-word, and the test asserts that behaviour. The stated invariant is inaccurate, though only for text with no whitespace at all.
attacks.evidence: "else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });" and "expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }]);"

attacks.claim: When a text token overflows after earlier content and contains no whitespace in its head, the whole token is dropped silently rather than cut, so a long unbroken word after other text disappears from the collapsed view.
attacks.evidence: "if (cut > 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: head.slice(0, cut) });\n      else if (out.length === 0) ..." with no branch for out.length > 0 and cut <= 0

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT strips a closing ')' even when it balances an opening '(' inside the URL, so some valid parenthesised URLs (e.g. wiki-style links) will be linked truncated.
